title: Singapore's Temasek Eyes IPL Franchise Stakes as Global Investor Rush Intensifies
excerpt: The sovereign wealth fund's managing director confirmed Temasek's interest in the Indian Premier League for the first time, as two franchise sales this year valued teams at over $1.6 billion each.
body:
Singapore's sovereign wealth fund Temasek is exploring investment in India's Indian Premier League cricket franchises, its top India executive told Reuters on Tuesday, marking the latest entry in an accelerating race among global institutional investors for a piece of the world's richest cricket tournament.

"IPL is a marquee property and we remain interested in it. For the right opportunity, we would jump on it."

— Vishesh Shrivastav, Managing Director, Temasek India

Shrivastav declined to name any specific franchise Temasek was evaluating but confirmed the fund's interest publicly for the first time, according to Reuters.

A League Transformed: From Bollywood to Blackstone

"The fund, which manages assets worth over $380 billion, has steadily expanded its India footprint."

The IPL, launched in 2008 as a playground for Bollywood stars and Indian business tycoons, has undergone a dramatic transformation in its ownership landscape. Two blockbuster franchise deals in 2026 alone have underscored the shift.

In March, United Spirits — the Indian subsidiary of British drinks giant Diageo — sold Royal Challengers Bengaluru to a four-member consortium for $1.78 billion. The buyer group includes the Aditya Birla Group, The Times of India Group, billionaire David Blitzer's Bolt Ventures, and Blackstone's perpetual private equity arm. Aryaman Vikram Birla was named chairman of the new ownership structure.

More recently, Kal Somani, a US-based Indian-origin technology entrepreneur from Scottsdale, Arizona, acquired Rajasthan Royals for $1.63 billion through a consortium that includes Walmart, according to Cricbuzz. The deal represented a staggering return — the Royals were purchased for just $67 million at the IPL's inaugural 2008 auction.

"The acquisition of Rajasthan Royals at $1.63 billion reinforces our view that IPL franchises are now valued in the $1.5 to $2.0 billion range, supported by strong media monetisation and rising global investor interest," said Karan Turani of Elara Capital.

Franchise Values and the Media Rights Engine

The IPL's total valuation crossed $18.5 billion in 2025, according to US-based investment bank Houlihan Lokey. That figure is powered by escalating media rights deals — the league's current broadcast cycle, sold in 2023, was valued at roughly $6.2 billion over five years, dwarfing most global cricket properties.

Temasek's interest adds another category of institutional capital to the mix. The fund, which manages assets worth over $380 billion, has steadily expanded its India footprint. Its India portfolio exposure has more than quadrupled over the past decade to $42 billion, with investments spanning Haldiram's, Manipal Hospitals, and positions across financial services, consumer goods, and healthcare, according to Reuters.

The fund's cricket interest also sits alongside its broader sports investment thesis. Several sovereign wealth funds in the Gulf and Southeast Asia have ramped up investments in global sports properties in recent years, from football clubs to Formula 1 teams.

Diaspora Investors Reshape the IPL

The recent ownership wave has a strong diaspora thread. Somani, an Indian-American entrepreneur who held a minority stake in the Royals since 2021, now leads the franchise from the United States. Blitzer, whose Bolt Ventures is part of the RCB consortium, is a prominent American sports investor with stakes in multiple US and European franchises. The growing involvement of global Indian-origin investors and multinational institutions signals the IPL's maturation into a mainstream alternative asset class with appeal far beyond India's borders.

What's Next

With Temasek now openly scouting opportunities, attention will turn to which franchise could be next to attract a deal. Several IPL teams are exploring global expansion through overseas T20 leagues, though RCB's new co-owner Satyan Gajwani recently told media the team has no immediate plans for international franchise expansion, preferring to consolidate its Bengaluru brand first. Meanwhile, the BCCI awaits its cut — five percent of each transaction, amounting to roughly ₹765 crore on the Rajasthan Royals deal alone. Whether Temasek targets an outright acquisition or a minority stake, its entry would further validate the IPL as a top-tier global sports investment.
